exposure: detectable perinatal risk factors and/or neonatal symptoms for cerebral palsy
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 1333 term-born children with cerebral palsy from the Canadian Cerebral Palsy Registry.
finding: One-quarter of term-born children with CP in the Canadian registry lacked neonatal encephalopathy, seizures, or perinatal risk factors, and they were more likely to have unilateral CP, focal MRI findings, and communicate with words than children with such risk factors or neonatal symptoms.
cross-section timing: Characteristics of children with CP, as recorded in the Canadian Cerebral Palsy Registry, at an unspecified point after birth.
